as_told.title: Schumer's bill mentions UAP and NHI 65 times

tellings.quote: SA 797. Mr. SCHUMER (for himself, Mr. Rounds, Mr. Rubio, Mrs. Gillibrand, Mr. Young, and Mr. Heinrich) submitted an amendment intended to be proposed by him to the bill S. 2226

(12) Non-human intelligence.--The term ``non-human intelligence'' means any sentient intelligent non-human lifeform regardless of nature or ultimate origin that may be presumed responsible for unidentified anomalous phenomena or of which the Federal Government has become aware.

(10) Legacy program.--The term ``legacy program'' means all Federal, State, and local government, commercial industry, academic, and private sector endeavors to collect, exploit, or reverse engineer technologies of unknown origin or examine biological evidence of living or deceased non-human intelligence that pre-dates the date of the enactment of this Act.

plain: In 2023 Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer put forward a bill that, the tellers say, wrote non-human technology and the recovery of crashed craft into the law of Congress. The whistleblower David Grusch tells Michels Schumer was 'compelled' to write a 'big 64 page amendment' about non-human tech and recoveries. The writer Marik von Rennenkampff asks how 'nonhuman intelligence' got into a bill also backed by Marco Rubio and Kirsten Gillibrand, and says it mentions the phrase 22 times along with biological evidence; Michels puts it at 65 mentions of UAP, the official word for UFOs, and NHI, short for non-human intelligence. Karl Nell, speaking as a former official, says the bill amounted to Congress saying it 'is not being told the truth', and Dan Sheehan, a guest who traces the history of American secret programs, says the law that came out of it, signed by the president, orders the military services to gather their UFO records back to 1945. The Congressional Record of 13 July 2023 prints the amendment, SA 797, as submitted by Schumer 'for himself, Mr. Rounds, Mr. Rubio, Mrs. Gillibrand, Mr. Young, and Mr. Heinrich' to the Senate's yearly defence bill. It defines non-human intelligence as 'any sentient intelligent non-human lifeform regardless of nature or ultimate origin', and defines a 'legacy program' as efforts to 'collect, exploit, or reverse engineer technologies of unknown origin or examine biological evidence of living or deceased non-human intelligence'. So the text does deal with recovered technology and biology, as the tellers say, though as definitions in a disclosure law rather than as a statement that such things exist. In that print it runs to seven pages and uses 'non-human intelligence' 24 times, and the tellers do not say which version gives their 64 pages or their counts.

discussion.by: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act of 2023 (SA 797 to S. 2226)
discussion.text: In the Congressional Record of 13 July 2023 the amendment Schumer submitted for himself, Rounds, Rubio, Gillibrand, Young and Heinrich is printed on seven pages (S2953 to S2959) and uses the phrase "non-human intelligence" 24 times, headings included. The tellers do not say which print of the amendment they mean by 64 pages, or what they counted (22 times, or 65 times with UAP); if it is this text, the count of the phrase alone is 24.
